study: Lewis Presser et al. 2015, Next Generation Preschool Math (NGPM) tablet-augmented curriculum, pre-k (SREE)
eval_evidence: Conference paper authored by the developers at EDC and SRI International (NSF DRL-1119118), who designed the NGPM curriculum and digital apps and ran the evaluation.
developer_evidence: Treatment teachers attended a full-day PD workshop run as part of the developer-led efficacy study (p.97); not stated to be delivered by an outside intermediary, so taken as developer/research-team delivered (medium confidence).
cascade_evidence: Single developer-run workshop to treatment teachers in a small 16-center efficacy trial; no train-the-trainer/lead-teacher hop described.
counterfactual_evidence: Control teachers continued business as usual and were 'provided the professional development and materials at the conclusion of the study' (waitlist BAU control) (p.102-103).
coaching_evidence: PD = a single full-day workshop prior to implementation (content, technology orientation, game/activity overview); no ongoing in-class coaching described (p.97-101).
student_dose_evidence: Each classroom received five iPads (four for children in a digital learning center) plus tablet-based math games children played directly (5:1 manipulatives-to-digital ratio, 8 digital games) - a substantial student-facing software dose beyond regular teacher instruction (p.92-102).
maturity_evidence: A single short (~6-week) supplemental math unit implementation; a discrete one-shot design with no multi-year maturation axis.
